google/gemini-2.5-flash.mistake: In the statement 'p_10(Braden) ⊕ p_3(Braden)' vs 'For Braden, finding a new passion and pursuing his original goal of becoming an Olympic gymnast are mutually exclusive.', the FOL operator `⊕` (exclusive OR) means that exactly one of the two propositions must be true, *and* they cannot both be true. The natural language phrase 'mutually exclusive' only means that both cannot be true simultaneously (i.e., `¬(p_10(Braden) ∧ p_3(Braden))`). It does not imply that one of them *must* be true. Hence, the FOL statement is stronger than what is conveyed by the NL.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: The formula p_10(Braden) ⊕ p_3(Braden) asserts exclusive OR (exactly one of p_10 or p_3 is true). The English “are mutually exclusive” only states they cannot both be true, but does not assert that one of them must be true. The correct translation of “mutually exclusive” would be ¬(p_10(Braden) ∧ p_3(Braden)) (which allows both to be false).
